verdicts.claim: The 'aura census' is the alpha enumeration in towerCover.test.ts — regex-extracts every `alpha:` from spawnerZoneRenderer.ts, pins the total at 6, requires each to end in a cover multiplier.
verdicts.note: Opened it. `src/render/towerCover.test.ts:324` `it('⛔ EVERY alpha the spawner aura draws with is scaled by a cover alpha — all six', () => {`; `:326` `const alphas = [...src.matchAll(/\balpha:\s*([^,}\n]+)/g)].map((m) => m[1]!.trim());`; `:328` `expect(alphas, ...).toHaveLength(6);`; `:330` `expect(a, \`un-covered alpha: ${a}\`).toMatch(/\*\s*(zoneAlpha|bondCover)$/);`. Quoted evidence is verbatim and the line numbers are exact.

verdicts.claim: Pixi does NOT require `alpha:` — it is optional, defaults to 1, and StrokeStyle inherits the same optional field.
verdicts.note: `node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/graphics/shared/FillTypes.d.ts:100` reads exactly `    alpha?: number;`, preceded at :96 by `     * @default 1`. `:393` reads `export interface StrokeStyle extends FillStyle, StrokeAttributes {`. Both line numbers are exact.

verdicts.claim: Omitting `alpha:` is the dominant idiom in this repo's renderers — both the object form without alpha and the bare-colour shorthand are in production files.
verdicts.note: `src/render/characterSheet.ts:339` `      .fill({ color: 0x101a26 })`; `src/render/codexOverlay.ts:547` `    this.viewportMask.rect(0, SCROLL_VIEW_TOP, CANVAS_WIDTH, SCROLL_VIEW_H).fill(0xffffff);`. I also counted the population the probe only asserted: 19 `.fill(0x…)` and 12 `.fill({ color: 0x… })` occurrences across non-test `src/render/*.ts`. The idiom claim is measured, not rhetorical.

verdicts.claim: CONSEQUENCE — the census is UNDER-strict: a seventh draw written as `.fill({ color: tint })` keeps the count at 6 and the loop finds nothing new, so the guard stays green over a fully-opaque redraw of a hidden connector.
verdicts.note: Follows mechanically from the two verified facts. The docblock it indicts is verbatim at `towerCover.test.ts:321-322`: `   * each to end in a cover multiplier. A seventh draw added without one turns this red before it` / `   * can ship over an invisible connector.` The regex is keyed on the `alpha:` PROPERTY, so a draw with no such property contributes nothing to `alphas` and the `toHaveLength(6)` pin does not move.

verdicts.claim: The docblock makes a claim it cannot keep, and the two statements of it disagree by one (:242 'a SIXTH un-scaled fill' vs :321 'a SEVENTH draw').
verdicts.note: `towerCover.test.ts:242` ` *    cover alpha. **A sixth un-scaled fill fails this test.** That is the S182 footer pattern` vs `:321` `a seventh draw added without one turns this red`. The ordinals do disagree, and both are wrong in the same direction. ⚠ The probe's arithmetic gloss is loose, though: `spawnerZoneRenderer.ts` today has 4 `.fill(` + 2 `.stroke(` = 6 draws carrying 6 alphas, so ':242 says a sixth... but six alphas already exist' conflates 'fill' with 'alpha'. The :242 'sixth' is carried over from the S182 footer's five-count it quotes in the same sentence. Substance holds; wording is sloppy.

verdicts.claim: The census is ALSO over-strict — `[^,}\n]+` stops at the first comma, so `alpha: Math.min(1, 0.4 * zoneAlpha)` captures as `Math.min(1` and fails the `$`-anchored match; a hoisted local and `alpha: zoneAlpha * 0.5` fail too.
verdicts.note: `towerCover.test.ts:326` capture class is literally `([^,}\n]+)` and `:330` asserts `.toMatch(/\*\s*(zoneAlpha|bondCover)$/)` — anchored at end-of-string on the trimmed capture. A clamp truncates at the comma; a hoisted `const a = 0.3 * zoneAlpha` yields the capture `a`; `zoneAlpha * 0.5` ends in `0.5`. All three are correct code that reddens this test.

verdicts.claim: A third hole: it pins the TEXT of the multiplier but not that it is the RIGHT cover for that geometry — a per-bond stroke scaled by `zoneAlpha` instead of `bondCover` passes.
verdicts.note: `src/render/spawnerZoneRenderer.ts:186` `          .stroke({ width: 1.5 + shimmer * 1.5, color: tint, alpha: bondAlpha * bondCover });`. corrections: ⛔ THE BIGGEST MISS, AND IT INVERTS THE REPORT'S OWN THESIS. The probe argues the census 'cannot see a new un-scaled draw' in `spawnerZoneRenderer.ts` — where all six alphas are correct today. It never looked at the OTHER cover consumer, which has THREE un-cover-scaled alphas RIGHT NOW and no census at all. `src/render/structureRenderer.ts:345` `const PATTERN_ALPHA = 0.45;`, drawn at `:408` `.stroke({ width: 1.5, color: PATTERN_COLOR, alpha: PATTERN_ALPHA });`, `:410` `g.circle(m.x, m.y, BEAD_RADIUS).fill({ color: PATTERN_COLOR, alpha: PATTERN_ALPHA });` and `:420` (chevron, same literal). The connector underneath fades — `:263` `alpha: 0.85 * coverAlpha,` — while the seat pattern on top does not. The gate is binary only: `:288` `if (colorToSeat !== null && coverAlpha > TOWER_COVER_DRAW_EPSILON) {`, and `TOWER_COVER_DRAW_EPSILON = 0.02` (`towerCover.ts:119`).

⛔ AND IT IS REACHABLE IN THE MAINLINE, NOT BEHIND A PREF. `structureRenderer.ts:193` `const patterned = world.gameMode !== 'solo';` — so this draws in EVERY multiplayer match. The ramp is continuous, not a step: `towerCover.ts:227-233` `const t = elapsed <= 0 ? 0 : elapsed >= span ? 1 : elapsed / span; return p.covered ? 1 - t : t;` over `TOWER_COVER_FADE_TICKS = 120` (`:98`) — two full seconds at 60 Hz, one second back (`TOWER_COVER_REVEAL_TICKS = 60`, `:116`). At coverAlpha 0.1 the connector renders at 0.085 and its decoration at a flat 0.45 — the ornament is five times brighter than the thing it ornaments. The in-file comment at `:284-287` justifies SKIPPING rather than fading, but only argues the alpha-0 case ('a phased-out connector would keep a fully opaque dash pattern floating where it used to be'); it never addresses mid-ramp. This is the owner's own complaint class ('you can still see the connectors') and it is live today, not hypothetical.

⚠ SECOND MISS — THE TEST DIRECTLY ABOVE THE CENSUS COMMITS THE SAME SIN THE REPORT INDICTS. `src/render/towerCover.test.ts:307` `it('⛔ exactly these renderers read a cover alpha, and every other one reads none', …)` — but `:312-313` enumerates only five files: `['towerRenderer.ts', 'voltkinTowerRenderer.ts', 'structureRampRenderer.ts', 'turretRenderer.ts', 'princessRenderer.ts']`. There are ~90 non-test files in `src/render/`. Its sibling PUBLISHERS negative at `:289-290` checks SEVEN. A sixth consumer appearing in any unlisted renderer is invisible to a test whose name asserts completeness. Any fix to the census should close this in the same edit — it is three lines and the same class of hole.

⚠ THE PROPOSED FIX'S CONTROL ARM IS THE WRONG HALF. `fix_shape` proposes asserting `.fill(0x` does not appear in the file. That catches only the hex-literal shorthand; `.fill(tint)` and `.stroke({ width, color })` with a variable colour slip straight past it. The load-bearing half is the DRAW-CALL COUNT, and I verified it pins cleanly: exactly 4 `.fill(` + 2 `.stroke(` in `spawnerZoneRenderer.ts` (:151, :163, :186, :191, :198, :202), with zero false positives from comments after `codeOf()` strips them. Pin 6 draw calls; treat the `.fill(0x` arm as decoration, not protection.

⚠ FIX_SHAPE OMISSION — the rename has more call sites than it lists. `scripts/check-atlas-scenery.mjs:102` `  console.error('usage: node scripts/check-atlas-scenery.mjs [--no-size] [--allow-scenery N] <dir> [<dir>...]');` already omits `--dark-bg` entirely — a pre-existing doc defect the probe did not find, and a line a rename must touch. And SPARK_CANON.md names the flag at FOUR lines (597, 600, 607, 609), not just the one table row the report says to append to.

⭐ A SCOPE CHECK THAT CAME BACK CLEAN — record it so the next session does not re-derive it. `src/canon.test.ts` does NOT pin the `--dark-bg` section (grep for `dark-bg|lightning-hub|STOPS GUARDING|atlas` returns zero hits), and `src/render/structureRamp.test.ts` does not source-text-assert its own module's docblock (its only `readFileSync` is at `:729`, against `../main.ts`). So editing `SPARK_CANON.md:597` and `structureRamp.ts:29` carries no hidden red. That is the one scope surprise this fix could have had, and it does not.

Correction to finding 13's wording: `--dark-bg` is not a 'threshold escape' — it deletes checks 3 and 5 outright (`darkBg ? [] : Object.entries(res)` at :451 and :465). The threshold widening is the separate `--allow-scenery 1500`. Two different defects with two different fixes; the report fuses them into one sentence and weakens both.

Correction to finding 5's arithmetic: ':242 says a SIXTH un-scaled fill fails — but six alphas already exist and pass' conflates fills with alphas. The file has 4 fills, 2 strokes, 6 alphas, 6 draws. The :242 'sixth' is inherited from the S182 footer's five-count that the very same sentence quotes. The off-by-one against :321 is real; the explanation given for it is not.
net_assessment:
THE REPORT SURVIVES THE AUDIT. 16 of 17 findings CONFIRMED verbatim at the cited line, 1 PARTIAL on wording only. Every file:line I opened said what the probe said it said — no fabricated symbols, no stale line numbers, no S120-class invention. I also verified two things it asserted without showing (the three sibling atlas-specs really do name the same alpha intake; `git log -S` really does put `--allow-scenery 1500` in db5c5d6, whose message greps 0 for either flag). Both findings are STILL LIVE at 7d1514b.

⛔ BUT IT AUDITED THE WRONG FILE FOR ITS OWN THESIS. Finding 3's argument is 'a census keyed on the `alpha:` property cannot see an un-scaled draw' — and it proves that about `spawnerZoneRenderer.ts`, where all six alphas are correct today and the risk is hypothetical. The other cover consumer, `structureRenderer.ts`, has THREE un-cover-scaled alphas shipping right now (`:408`, `:410`, `:420`, all `alpha: PATTERN_ALPHA` = 0.45 at `:345`) over a connector that fades at `0.85 * coverAlpha` (`:263`), reachable in every non-solo match (`:193`), for the full 120-tick fade (`towerCover.ts:98`) — and it has no census at all. The hand-run grep the project's own CLAUDE.md calls the cheapest lane ('enumerate every production call site and ask who can reach each one') found this in one command and the probe did not run it. That is the finding with teeth, and it is not in the report.

GRADING THE ESTIMATES. `four_sites_risk: NONE` is CORRECT and I checked rather than accepted it: neither fix touches factory/serialize/hash/worker, `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 47, nothing reaches the sim, and `spawnerZoneRenderer`'s only wall-clock (`performance.now()` at `:77`) is render-only and documented at `:18-21`. The named CI surface is right too — `.github/workflows/e2e.yml:215` `atlas-guard:` → `:241` `run: npm run check:atlas` — so a rename must land in script and package.json in one commit.

`size_estimate: Micro each, Micro-to-Standard combined` is FAIR BUT LIGHT, and light in three specific ways, none fatal: (a) the rename ripples to `check-atlas-scenery.mjs:102` and four canon lines, not one table row; (b) if the missed `structureRenderer` alphas are folded in — and they should be, since they are the same edit in the same feature and the report's own §5 triage rule says a merge owner does these once rather than round-tripping — that is a second test file plus three production lines; (c) the one honest unknown the report DOES flag stands: whether the pentagram passes checks 3/5 without the exemption cannot be settled read-only (needs numpy/scipy/Pillow), and a dirty result turns Finding 4 from a rename into an art decision that is the owner's. Call it Standard if the structureRenderer fix rides along, Micro-to-Standard if it does not.

VERDICT ON 'worth a session': I agree with the report's own recommendation and would strengthen it. Neither deserves a session alone. But the structureRenderer defect I found is not a contract defect — it is a live visual one in the exact class the owner has personally reported across eight sessions, and it should ride the connector-hiding work (item 2 on his list) as a fix, not as a doc note.
